web-pages.admin.code.linkHint: Sign in through this link and the code is filled in when creating a workspace.

web-pages.admin.code.madeLead.one: Send the code or sign-up link to them. It can be used once and expires in 1 day.
web-pages.admin.code.madeLead.other: Send the code or sign-up link to them. It can be used once and expires in {n} days.

web-pages.admin.code.makeLead: They sign in to still.fail and use it to create a workspace; from then on that account may create up to 5. A code can be used once. For people who have already signed in, grant it on their user page instead.
web-pages.admin.code.noteHint: Optional: who it's for, to recognize it later.
web-pages.admin.code.notePlaceholder: e.g. For Alex on the product team
web-pages.admin.code.revokeBody: Once revoked, this code can no longer be used to create a workspace. Sign-up links already sent stop working too.
web-pages.admin.fb.copied: Copied. Ready to paste to an agent
web-pages.admin.noFeedback: This still.fail cloud doesn't take feedback yet
web-pages.admin.noPermission.title: No permission
web-pages.admin.search.codes: Search code, note, who used it
web-pages.admin.search.feedback: Search title, content, reporter, station, workspace, FB number
web-pages.admin.signIn.lead: Only {name} admins can use this. Sign in with an admin Google account.
web-pages.admin.signIn.title: {name} admin
web-pages.admin.title: Admin
web-pages.admin.user.blockBody: They're signed out on all devices at once and can't sign in again. Workspaces and their contents stay as they are. You can unblock at any time.
web-pages.admin.ws.deleteBody: All members are removed, and its stations disconnect and need to join another workspace. This can't be undone.
web-pages.appearance.language.descriptio: The language of the interface. Following the system uses this device's language.
web-pages.appearance.theme.description: Light, dark, or match the system. Applies to this browser only.
web-pages.appearance.theme.title: Theme
web-pages.appearance.title: Appearance
web-pages.archive.about: Chats archived by hand, and finished chats idle for over a day (not running, not stopped at a block, nothing unread). A chat returns to the list by itself when there's a new message.
web-pages.archive.deleteText: Its session, chat history and workspace folder will be deleted. This can't be undone.
web-pages.archive.title: Archived
web-pages.chat.pickSaved: Changed. Takes effect from the next turn
web-pages.cloud.cantOpenBody: None of your signed-in accounts are in it.
web-pages.cloud.inviteOnlyBody: If you have an invite code, enter it below to create your own workspace. Or ask someone already using {name} to invite {email} to their workspace.
web-pages.cloud.inviteSignIn: You've been invited to a {name} workspace. Sign in with Google first, then decide whether to join.
web-pages.cloud.noWorkspace: You're not in any workspace yet
web-pages.cloud.noWorkspaceBody: Ask someone already using {name} to invite {email} to their workspace, or create your own.
web-pages.cloud.signInWithCode: You have a {name} invite code. Sign in with Google to create your own workspace.
web-pages.cloud.slackInstalled.doneBody: Back in {name}, the app is waiting on the Connect page. Add its App-Level Token to connect. You can close this page.
web-pages.cloud.slackInstalled.handing: Handing the install to the station…
web-pages.cloud.slackInstalled.notInstal: The app wasn't allowed in Slack. Go back to {name} and click “Install to Workspace” again.
web-pages.cloud.slackInstalled.signInBod: Sign in with the account that created this app so the install can be handed to the station. Then click “Install to Workspace” in {name} again.
web-pages.connect.bindSaved: Saved. New sessions use the new settings
web-pages.connect.bothRuntimes: This model runs on both runtimes. The runtime can't change after creation.
web-pages.connect.chooseLead: From now on, messages to “{name}” go into the chosen session. The previous session is kept but gets no new messages from this connect.
web-pages.connect.deleteBody: It will disconnect from Slack. You'll need to delete the app in Slack yourself.

web-pages.connect.deleteBodySessions.one: It will disconnect from Slack. Its 1 session keeps its history but gets no new messages. You'll need to delete the app in Slack yourself.
web-pages.connect.deleteBodySessions.other: It will disconnect from Slack. Its {n} sessions keep their history but get no new messages. You'll need to delete the app in Slack yourself.

web-pages.connect.effects.mentionOnly: From now on, only @-mentioned threads go into the session. Replies in threads already in it still arrive.
web-pages.connect.effects.newSingle: The next message starts a new single session; you can also pick an existing session after switching.
web-pages.connect.effects.noMention: No @ needed: every message in all channels and DMs it can see goes to the agent, which uses noticeably more.
web-pages.connect.effects.resumeSingle: It picks up the single session it was bound to before.

web-pages.connect.effects.running.one: 1 session is running now. It will finish its current turn.
web-pages.connect.effects.running.other: {n} sessions are running now. They will finish their current turn.

web-pages.connect.effects.switchBack: Switching back to single session later picks up the same session.
web-pages.connect.effects.threadsRestart: To continue a thread from the single session, @ it again. That opens a new session without the earlier context.
web-pages.connect.effects.toMulti: The bound session stops getting new messages. From now on, each thread gets its own new session when @-mentioned.
web-pages.connect.effects.toSingle: From now on, all messages it gets go into one session. Existing per-thread sessions stop getting new messages, including replies in those threads. History is kept.
web-pages.connect.everyMessageSentence: Every message it can see goes into the session.
web-pages.connect.made.appToken: Generate an App-Level Token on the Socket Mode page and copy it (starts with xapp-; scopes are already chosen).
web-pages.connect.made.manual: The app is created. Install it to the workspace, then copy the Bot User OAuth Token (starting with xoxb-) from the OAuth page.
web-pages.connect.made.oauth: The app is created. Install it to the workspace: click “Allow” in Slack and the bot token goes to the station automatically.
web-pages.connect.manualApp: Create the app in Slack yourself and paste its tokens
web-pages.connect.manualShort: Create the app yourself, without a configuration token
web-pages.connect.mentionOff: Every message it can see in channels goes into the session.
web-pages.connect.mentionOn: Later replies in an @-mentioned thread don't need another @.
web-pages.connect.modeLead: This changes which session each message goes into from now on. Ongoing conversations may be cut off, so check the effects below before confirming.
web-pages.connect.noModels: No models enabled in profiles · Enable some
web-pages.connect.noModelsFor: No models enabled in {runtime} profiles · Enable some
web-pages.connect.noSession: No session yet. The next message starts a new one.
web-pages.connect.noToken: Rather not use a configuration token?
web-pages.connect.ownerLead: The owner decides whose “Created by me” it shows in. Only owners, admins and the current owner can change it.
web-pages.connect.recentNone: No sessions yet. @{name} in Slack to start one.
web-pages.connect.replaceLead: You can replace just one. Leave the other empty to keep the saved one.
web-pages.connect.runtimeNote: Runs on {runtime}, which can't change after creation. For another runtime, create a new connect. Sessions in progress keep the settings they started with.
web-pages.connect.slackLead: This connect isn't connected to Slack yet.
web-pages.connect.step.firstToken: Get a Slack configuration token first
web-pages.connect.teamLead: Which Slack workspace's configuration token to create the app with.
web-pages.connect.tokenWhy: With it, {name} creates the app in Slack for you: fill in its name, avatar and permissions here instead of setting each up in Slack. It's yours only. Others on this station can't see it.
web-pages.connects.about: A connect is where people reach {name}, such as a Slack app. Each connect lives on a station and is bound to a model.
web-pages.connects.addFirstLead: A connect lets people @ an agent in Slack: a Slack app hooked up to a station.
web-pages.connects.installedNeedsToken: Installed in “{team}”, needs an App-Level Token
web-pages.connects.noOnline: No station is online. Add one once it's online.
web-pages.connects.notInstalled: Not installed to a workspace yet
web-pages.connects.profileFirstLead: Connects use a profile to run models. Add one, then come back to add a connect.
web-pages.connects.removeBody: Removes it from {name} only. The app stays in Slack; delete it from Slack's app settings if you no longer need it.
web-pages.decisions.title: Decisions
web-pages.errors.inviteCodeInvalid: This invite code isn't valid. Check it for typos
web-pages.errors.inviteCodeRequired: Creating a workspace needs an invite code. Joining someone else's workspace doesn't
web-pages.errors.inviteCodeUsed: This invite code has already been used
web-pages.errors.tooManyMembers: A workspace can invite up to 5 people
web-pages.errors.tooManyWorkspaces: An account can create up to 5 workspaces
web-pages.notifications.denied: The browser blocked notifications. Turn them on in the browser's site settings
web-pages.notifications.noteBrowser: Notifies you when an agent in a chat you're in finishes, needs you, hits an error, or someone speaks. Not for the chat you're viewing. Applies to this browser only
web-pages.notifications.noteDevice: Notifies you when an agent in a chat you're in finishes, needs you, hits an error, or someone speaks. Not for the chat you're viewing. Applies to this device only (also allow {name} to send notifications in System Settings)
web-pages.notifications.title: Chat notifications
web-pages.profiles.background: Move running commands to the background when a new message arrives
web-pages.profiles.backgroundOff: New messages are read only after the running command or subagent finishes.
web-pages.profiles.backgroundOn: While Claude Code waits on a command or subagent, a new message moves them to the background (like pressing Ctrl+B). The agent reads the message right away and handles the results when they finish.
web-pages.profiles.choice.anthropicApiLe: An Anthropic API key, runs Claude Code.
web-pages.profiles.choice.chatgptSubLead: ChatGPT Plus / Pro, runs Codex. Sign in once with a device code.
web-pages.profiles.choice.claudeSubLead: Claude Pro / Max, runs Claude Code. Sign in once in the browser.
web-pages.profiles.choice.envLead: Set the environment variables for your model service yourself.
web-pages.profiles.choice.opencodeGoLead: One key for both Claude Code and Codex.
web-pages.profiles.copyFailed: Couldn't copy the code. Please type it in
web-pages.profiles.copyOpen: Copy code and open sign-in page
web-pages.profiles.deleteBody: Removes it from {name}'s settings only. The config folder and the sign-in in it aren't deleted.
web-pages.profiles.deviceCodeNote: On the OpenAI page that opens, sign in with the ChatGPT account {name} should use and paste the code. This continues by itself once done. If the page says device code sign-in is off, turn it on in ChatGPT's security settings first.
web-pages.profiles.disableBody: {name} stops using this machine's {runtime} sign-in. The sign-in on this machine isn't affected and can be used again later.
web-pages.profiles.envLead: The runtime starts with these variables to reach your model service. {route} in a value is replaced with the session's route ID.
web-pages.profiles.envSaved: Saved {masked}. Leave empty to keep it
web-pages.profiles.fastLead: Sessions that follow the subscription use this. Fast uses more quota or credits
web-pages.profiles.keychainTip: This sign-in is in a keychain the station can't read, so it can't be used directly. Sign in once for {name}; the machine's own sign-in isn't affected
web-pages.profiles.lead: What agents use to run models: {subscription} or a key for a model service.
web-pages.profiles.machineAdded: Profile added, using this machine's sign-in
web-pages.profiles.machineLoginAbout: To switch accounts, sign in again or sign out, do it in {runtime} on this machine and this profile follows. To stop using it, disable it (menu at top right).
web-pages.profiles.machineSignedIn: Already signed in on this machine
web-pages.profiles.manual: Or sign in by hand on the server
web-pages.profiles.modelsAbout: Only enabled models can be picked in new chats and connects.
web-pages.profiles.modelsAboutNone: Once the profile is checked, its models are listed here. Enable them to use them.
web-pages.profiles.name: Name
web-pages.profiles.signInNote: Sign-in happens on the machine running {name}; you only authorize in the browser.
web-pages.profiles.signedInSwitch: Signed in. To switch accounts, sign in again.
web-pages.profiles.signingInNote: Finish within 15 minutes, or it's cancelled automatically.
web-pages.profiles.step1: Open the authorization page, sign in with the Claude account {name} should use, and approve.
web-pages.profiles.step2: After you approve, the page shows an authorization code. Copy it here:
web-pages.profiles.subscriptionNote: Sign-in happens on the machine running {name}; you only authorize in the browser. The profile is added once sign-in succeeds.
web-pages.profiles.useMachineTip: Uses this machine's sign-in directly, no need to sign in again. If you switch accounts or sign out on this machine, it follows
web-pages.profiles.usedByNone: No connects use this profile yet.
web-pages.roles.adminHint: Invites members, adds and removes stations
web-pages.roles.ownerHint: Manages everything, including member roles and deleting the workspace
web-pages.settings.account.sessionsLead: The browsers and devices where this account is signed in to {name}. Sign out any you don't recognize.
web-pages.settings.account.signOutConfir: This browser stops using this account, and its workspaces disappear from here. Other signed-in accounts aren't affected.
web-pages.settings.account.signOutHere: Sign out of {email} in this browser
web-pages.settings.account.signOutHereBo: Its workspaces disappear from here. Other signed-in accounts aren't affected.
web-pages.settings.enroll.about: Works on macOS (Apple silicon) and Linux. Use the same command on machines that already have {name}.
web-pages.settings.enroll.run: Run this in a terminal on that machine
web-pages.settings.enroll.waiting: Waiting for the machine to join
web-pages.settings.enroll.waitingNote: Continues by itself once the command runs · Valid for 1 hour
web-pages.settings.members.addLead: Added straight to “{workspace}”, no acceptance needed. People who've signed in to {name} become members right away; others join the first time they sign in with that email.

web-pages.settings.members.addedNote.one: 1 person · Joins on first sign-in to {name}
web-pages.settings.members.addedNote.other: {n} people · Join on first sign-in to {name}

web-pages.settings.members.doneAdded.one: 1 person will join on first sign-in to {name}
web-pages.settings.members.doneAdded.other: {n} people will join on first sign-in to {name}

web-pages.settings.members.emailsHint: The Google account email they use for {name}. You can paste several at once.
web-pages.settings.memory.lead: Memory shared by all chats on each station: global memory for things across projects, and one project memory per project. Memory stays on each station and isn't synced between them.
web-pages.settings.memory.offline: Offline. Check back once it's online.
web-pages.settings.memory.title: Memory
web-pages.settings.prices.lead: The unit prices each station uses to estimate cost
web-pages.settings.prices.title: Prices
web-pages.settings.profiles.lead: A profile is the account agents use to run models: a subscription, or a key for a model service. Each profile runs on its station, and {name} sets up which runtimes it can use.
web-pages.settings.profiles.offlineAdd: Offline. Add one once it's online
web-pages.settings.profiles.offlineNone: Offline. Its profiles haven't been read yet.
web-pages.settings.stations.addLead: Give it a name, then run a command on that machine.
web-pages.settings.stations.joined: “{name}” has joined. You can open it now.
web-pages.settings.stations.lead: Each station is a machine running {name}. Its connects, chats and profiles live on that machine.
web-pages.settings.stations.noneYet: This workspace has no stations yet. Wait for an admin to add one.
web-pages.settings.stations.removeConfir: It will disconnect from {name} cloud and members can no longer reach it from here. {name} and the data on that machine aren't affected, and you can add it again later.
web-pages.settings.thisMac.joined: This Mac has joined. It will show up in the list shortly
web-pages.settings.title: Settings
web-pages.settings.usage.lead: How many tokens the agents on each station used, priced at API rates, broken down by person, chat, account and model. Everyone in the workspace can see it.
web-pages.settings.usage.title: Usage
web-pages.settings.workspace.deleteBody: All members lose access and stations disconnect from {name} cloud. Data on the stations themselves isn't affected.

web-pages.settings.workspace.deleteConfi.one: All members will lose access, and 1 station will disconnect from {name} cloud (data on the station itself isn't affected).
web-pages.settings.workspace.deleteConfi.other: All members will lose access, and {n} stations will disconnect from {name} cloud (data on the stations themselves isn't affected).

web-pages.settings.workspace.leaveBody: You'll lose access to its stations until you're invited again.
web-pages.settings.workspace.leaveConfir: You'll lose access to its stations and need a new invitation to come back.
web-pages.settings.workspace.name: Name
web-pages.settings.workspace.nameHint: Only owners and admins can rename it.
web-pages.signIn.lead: Sign in with Google to manage your workspaces and their stations.
web-pages.signIn.title: Sign in to {name}
web-pages.slackApp.accessToken: That's the Access Token. The one needed is the Refresh Token below it, starting with xoxe-1-.
web-pages.slackApp.approveNote: Permissions changed. Slack needs your approval before they take effect.
web-pages.slackApp.descriptionPlaceholde: Description, shown on the app's profile
web-pages.slackApp.group.base.descriptio: Get messages when @-mentioned, read messages in its channels, DMs and group chats, and reply. Required.
web-pages.slackApp.group.canvases.descri: Create, edit and read canvases, such as writing plans and reports as canvases in a channel.
web-pages.slackApp.group.channels.descri: Create channels, invite members, and know when someone joins or creates a channel.
web-pages.slackApp.group.connect.descrip: View, send and accept invitations to channels shared with other companies.
web-pages.slackApp.group.customize: Post with another name and avatar
web-pages.slackApp.group.customize.descr: Each message can use its own display name and avatar.
web-pages.slackApp.group.dm.description: Open DMs with one or more people.
web-pages.slackApp.group.extras.descript: Unfurl links, set reminders, read Do Not Disturb and call status.
web-pages.slackApp.group.files.descripti: Read attachments in messages, upload screenshots, logs and other files.
web-pages.slackApp.group.lists.descripti: Create, edit and read Slack Lists, such as keeping a task list.
web-pages.slackApp.group.more.descriptio: Set its own presence, read message metadata and workspace settings, embed video links, respond to slash commands.
web-pages.slackApp.group.people.descript: Read emails, profiles, user groups, workspace info and custom emoji.
web-pages.slackApp.group.public: Post in public channels it hasn't joined
web-pages.slackApp.group.public.descript: Reply in public channels without being invited first.
web-pages.slackApp.group.reactions.descr: Mark progress with emoji, pin messages, manage channel bookmarks.
web-pages.slackApp.group.search.descript: Search messages and files in public channels and find people by name, to find context when answering.
web-pages.slackApp.group.topics: Set channel topics and invite members
web-pages.slackApp.group.topics.descript: Set the topic and purpose of channels and DMs, and invite people to channels.
web-pages.slackApp.group.usergroups: Manage user groups and start calls
web-pages.slackApp.group.usergroups.desc: Create user groups, change members, start and update Slack calls.
web-pages.slackApp.loading: Loading the app's settings from Slack…
web-pages.slackApp.needsToken: To edit the app here, you need your app configuration token for this Slack workspace.
web-pages.slackApp.needsTokenNote: It's yours only. Others on this station can't see it.
web-pages.slackApp.noApp: Can't find this connect's Slack app ({error}). Come back after switching to a valid token.
web-pages.slackApp.notConnected: Once connected to Slack, you can edit its app here.
web-pages.slackApp.refreshPrefix: The Refresh Token starts with xoxe-1-.
web-pages.slackApp.step1Note: Sign in with an account in the Slack workspace the bot goes into.
web-pages.slackApp.step2Note: Scroll to “Your App Configuration Tokens” at the bottom of the page, click Generate Token, and pick this workspace.
web-pages.slackApp.step3Note: Slack gives two tokens; use the lower one, starting with xoxe-1-. {name} renews it by itself, so you won't need to again.
web-pages.slackApp.updatedApprove: Updated. Takes effect once you approve the new permissions in Slack
web-pages.stations.away: Offline: open {name} on that machine and it will reconnect
web-pages.stations.neverConnected: Never connected: open {name} on that machine
web-pages.stations.silent: Not responding: {name} cloud says it's online, but its status can't be read. The machine may be offline or asleep
web-pages.stations.softwareOffline: Station offline. Updates show once it connects
web-pages.version.lead: Checks automatically at launch and every 4 hours. When there's a new version, “Update” appears at the top of the sidebar
web-pages.version.title: {name} desktop
web-pages.workspace.codeHint: {name} is invite-only for now. This account hasn't been invited to any workspace, so creating one needs an invite code.
web-pages.workspace.createLead: A workspace is a group of people and the stations they share. You'll be its owner.
web-pages.workspace.empty.body: Add one in {link}: just run a command on the machine that will run {name}.
web-pages.workspace.empty.title: This workspace has no stations yet
web-pages.workspace.noSuchStation: This station isn't in this workspace.
web-pages.workspace.onboarding.lead: Agents work on your machines. Start by adding a Mac or Linux machine.
web-pages.workspace.onboarding.title: Add your first station
